newsitem.title: MALAWI: Malawi President Muluzi to take 10 pct wage cut.
newsitem.headline: Malawi President Muluzi to take 10 pct wage cut.

text.p: The Malawi government said on Wednesday it would begin trimming its civil service in April and cut the salaries of President Bakili Muluzi and his cabinet ministers by 10 percent.
It said this was in line with a reform programme aimed at increasing government effeciency and cutting public spending.

Presdent Muluzi, who earns 25,000 kwacha ($1,667) per month has agreed to take a 10 percent salary cut and has ordered that his deputy Justin Malewezi and cabinet ministers do the same to show that the government is serious about cutting public expenditure.

Secretary to the president and cabinet, Alfred Upindi, told Malawi radio that downsizing the civil service would begin by cutting the jobs of 12 of a total of 60 principal secretaries who are either above 55 years or have served the government for more than 20 years.

"You will recall that members of the public have been complaining that there are too many principal secretaries in government and therefore a decision has been taken by my office to reduce the size of the civil Service," Upindi said.

"And this is the first step by reducing the number of principal secretaries by a certain number, so that after we have done various movements in the civil service the net result will be that the senior ranks will be reduced by 12," he said
A commission of inquiry report on Malawi's public service recommends that the jobs of 30,000 employees be cut so that the government can afford salary increases in the 1997/98 fiscal year.
The World Bank said last week the government did not have resources to cushion more than a billion kwacha in new wage bills for the public service if it went ahead with across-the-board increases.
